findings.highlight: I don't have that kind of money
findings.evidenceJa: そんな余分な金は使わない
findings.governingReading: He says he will not spend extra money, then turns to his real concern about girls walking at night.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s refusal to spend unnecessary money becomes inability to afford the taxi.

findings.highlight: If anyone picks a fight with Saber, they're dead for sure.
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーに手を出したらそれこそ返り討ちだろう
findings.governingReading: Anyone who lays a hand on Saber would instead be defeated by her.
findings.explanation: An attacker being beaten by Saber in a counterattack becomes certain death.

findings.highlight: if someone assaulted us
findings.evidenceJa: わたしたちが痴漢に襲われたら
findings.governingReading: She teases that Shirou meant he would rescue them if they were attacked by a molester.
findings.explanation: Rin’s concrete joke about molesters becomes generic assault.

findings.highlight: I walk a little faster and took the side path.
findings.evidenceJa: 早足で横道に入った
findings.governingReading: Shirou speeds up and enters the side path because walking beside both girls feels uncomfortable.
findings.explanation: The sentence changes tense from “walk” to “took.”

findings.highlight: walking right beside her
findings.evidenceJa: 二人と肩を並べて歩く
findings.governingReading: Shirou resists walking abreast of Rin and Saber together.
findings.explanation: Discomfort at walking shoulder to shoulder with both girls is narrowed to walking beside one “her.”

findings.highlight: What is in your head, Shirou? Stop thinking about such stupid crap.
findings.evidenceJa: 馬鹿らしい。なに考えてんだ、俺
findings.governingReading: He internally calls his own thoughts ridiculous and asks himself what he is thinking.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s first-person self-rebuke becomes a second-person voice addressing him by name.

findings.highlight: The priest must have incredible authority
findings.evidenceJa: ここの神父はよほどの人格者と見える
findings.governingReading: Because so many people visit a church entrusted to him, Shirou assumes the priest is highly virtuous.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s inference that the priest must be a person of exceptional character becomes a claim of institutional authority.

findings.highlight: The two have nothing in common.
findings.evidenceJa: この二つは似て非なる者
findings.governingReading: The Association and Church are alike in some respects but fundamentally different, publicly allied while ready to kill each other.
findings.explanation: Two organizations that are similar yet distinct become organizations with nothing in common.

findings.highlight: he's definitely an agent
findings.evidenceJa: バリッバリの代行者
findings.governingReading: Rin identifies Kotomine as a Holy Church Executor while mocking whether he has divine favor.
findings.explanation: The specialized Church role 代行者 is reduced to “agent.”

findings.highlight: he's a complete amateur. It's frustrating as hell.
findings.evidenceJa: 中身はてんで素人だから見てられなくって
findings.governingReading: She brought him because his complete inexperience was too painful to watch.
findings.explanation: Rin being unable to bear watching Shirou’s amateur state becomes personal frustration.

findings.highlight: This is a pity.
findings.evidenceJa: これは重症だ
findings.governingReading: On learning Shirou knows nothing, Kotomine diagnoses the situation as severe.
findings.explanation: Kotomine calling Shirou’s condition a serious case becomes pity.

findings.highlight: permeate in my mind, staining me like blood
findings.evidenceJa: 胸に浸透して、どろりと、血のように粘り着く
findings.governingReading: Despite making little rational sense, the words penetrate his chest unpleasantly and stick with the viscosity of blood.
findings.explanation: Kotomine’s words soaking into Shirou’s chest and clinging thickly like blood become staining his mind.

findings.highlight: one the greatest sacred relics
findings.evidenceJa: 聖遺物の中でも最高位
findings.governingReading: The Holy Grail is considered among the highest sacred relics.
findings.explanation: “One the greatest” omits “of.”

findings.highlight: and then each against the other to select the sole bearer.
findings.evidenceJa: 彼らを競わせてただ一人の持ち主を選定する
findings.governingReading: The Grail selects worthy candidates and sets them against one another to choose a sole owner.
findings.explanation: The description of the Grail making candidates compete loses its verb.

findings.highlight: that is one way to look about it.
findings.evidenceJa: そういう考えもできるか
findings.governingReading: Kotomine acknowledges Shirou’s relieved interpretation as one possible way to view the rule.
findings.explanation: “One way to look about it” uses the wrong preposition.

findings.highlight: a fool as well as a coward
findings.evidenceJa: 半人前どころか、ただの腑抜け
findings.governingReading: Kotomine taunts that such a mage would fall below half-fledged status and be merely gutless.
findings.explanation: A prospective quitter being not merely half-trained but spineless becomes both a fool and a coward.

findings.highlight: one of my most important responsibilities
findings.evidenceJa: 監督役として最優先事項
findings.governingReading: Kotomine calls protection of magi who cease being Masters the foremost priority of his office.
findings.explanation: Protecting former Masters is reduced from the overseer’s highest priority to one of several important duties.

findings.highlight: This church is a special agency
findings.evidenceJa: 特務局の末端
findings.governingReading: This church is at the end of a special department charged with relic recovery.
findings.explanation: The church as a peripheral outpost of a special bureau becomes the special agency itself.

findings.highlight: the Holy Grail observed in this town, which triggered a Holy Grail War
findings.evidenceJa: この町で観測される聖杯であり、聖杯戦争だ
findings.governingReading: Kotomine identifies one observed Grail in this town together with the recurring contest around it.
findings.explanation: The town’s observed Grail and its Holy Grail War become a Grail that triggered the War.

findings.highlight: I'm hoping to finally confuse him with this question.
findings.evidenceJa: 微かな期待をこめて問う
findings.governingReading: He asks with a small measure of hope that the overseer might restrain a dangerous victor.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s faint hope that Kotomine will answer his moral concern becomes hope that he can confuse Kotomine.

findings.highlight: Kotomine just laughs condescendingly.
findings.evidenceJa: 慇懃な仕草でおかしそうに笑った
findings.governingReading: As Shirou expected, Kotomine responds with polished formality and an amused smile.
findings.explanation: Kotomine’s formally courteous gesture and amused laugh become condescension.

findings.highlight: This guy is just so hard to deal with.
findings.evidenceJa: こいつの言葉は暴力みたいだ
findings.governingReading: The priest’s relentless use of facts feels physically violent to Shirou.
findings.explanation: Shirou compares Kotomine’s words to violence; English only calls him difficult to deal with.

findings.highlight: I lose my focus and I can't concentrate.
findings.evidenceJa: 焦点を失って、視点が定まらなくなる
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s sight blurs; visual focus and viewpoint cease to settle.
findings.explanation: Loss of visual focal stability becomes inability to concentrate mentally.

findings.highlight: I grit my teeth to maintain my composure.
findings.evidenceJa: 歯を噛みしめて意識を保つ
findings.governingReading: He braces himself and holds onto consciousness before collapsing.
findings.explanation: Shirou gritting his teeth to remain conscious becomes maintaining composure.

findings.highlight: Tohsaka to be concerned about the likes of me
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂がこういった心配をしてくれる
findings.governingReading: Shirou finds it extraordinarily rare for Tohsaka to express concern in this way.
findings.explanation: Rin showing this kind of concern becomes concern “about the likes of me.”

findings.highlight: don't beat me up too much
findings.evidenceJa: あんまりいじめないでくれ
findings.governingReading: He thanks her sincerely while continuing the playful complaint after one light smack.
findings.explanation: Shirou asks Rin not to tease or pick on him much; English asks her not to beat him up.

findings.highlight: I'm sure he knows exactly what I want to ask, but he urges me on anyway."
findings.evidenceJa: 俺が訊きたい事なんて見抜いているだろうに
findings.governingReading: Shirou thinks Kotomine probably already knows his question.
findings.explanation: A stray closing quotation mark appears after internal narration.

findings.highlight: the Holy Grail which temporary turned real
findings.evidenceJa: 一時的に本物となった聖杯
findings.governingReading: Kotomine describes the vessel becoming temporarily real through invocation.
findings.explanation: “Which temporary turned real” uses an adjective where an adverb is required.

findings.highlight: Seven Servants appear
findings.evidenceJa: 七人のサーヴァントが揃い
findings.governingReading: Kotomine says the Grail manifests after all seven Servants are present and time passes.
findings.explanation: Seven Servants being assembled becomes seven Servants appearing.

findings.highlight: It led to my father's death.
findings.evidenceJa: 父はその折に亡くなった
findings.governingReading: He says his father died on that occasion; afterward Kotomine inherited the overseer role.
findings.explanation: Kotomine’s father dying at that time becomes a death caused by the improper Master selection.

findings.highlight: There is reverence in his voice, and I see the devotion in his eyes before he turns.
findings.evidenceJa: その視線の先には、礼拝されるべき象徴が聳えている
findings.governingReading: After Kotomine turns away, a symbol worthy of worship towers in the direction of his gaze.
findings.explanation: A towering religious symbol becomes reverence in Kotomine's voice and devotion in his eyes. This adds an appearance of piety that the Japanese leaves unstated.

findings.highlight: The only thing you can decide beforehand is whether to prepare yourself
findings.evidenceJa: 決定されていた物があるとすれば、それは心構えが出来ていたかいないかだけ
findings.governingReading: Master selection itself was not guaranteed; the only settled distinction was whether the candidate had prepared mentally.
findings.explanation: The only predetermined difference being preparedness becomes something a person can decide beforehand.
